originalTitle: SC stays CIC order declaring NSEI 'public authority' under RTI Act
simplifiedContent: The Supreme Court has temporarily stopped a decision that would have forced the National Stock Exchange of India (NSEI) to share information with the public. This decision was made because the NSEI was considered a "public authority", which means it would have to provide information to citizens who ask for it. The NSEI didn't agree with this classification and asked for a review. A lower court had already agreed with the NSEI, but the Central Information Commission had said the opposite. This stay means that, for now, the NSEI doesn't have to share information with the public, but the final decision has not been made yet.

originalTitle: Quote of the day by Michael Price: "When people are looking for performance they sharpen their pencils and find reasons to buy"
simplifiedContent: Michael Price, an investor, said that when people want to make money, they carefully look for reasons to invest in certain companies. This means that investors should do their homework and thoroughly research a company's basics, such as its worth and potential for growth, before putting in their money. This careful research is important for finding companies that will do well over time. By being patient and taking the time to carefully evaluate companies, investors can increase their chances of finding successful investments. This approach can help investors make good choices, regardless of what's happening in the market.

originalTitle: Bloomberg delays India bonds inclusion in global index as investors seek proof reforms work
simplifiedContent: Bloomberg, a company that tracks investments, was thinking about adding Indian government bonds to its list of global investments. However, they decided to wait because they want to see if recent changes to India's financial system are working well for foreign investors. They acknowledged that India has made some progress in making it easier for foreigners to buy and sell bonds, but they want to see if these changes can be implemented smoothly. This decision matters because being included in the Bloomberg index can attract more foreign investors to India's bonds. By waiting, Bloomberg is essentially seeking proof that India's reforms are effective before giving its stamp of approval.

originalTitle: Exxon Mobil Q2 profit more than doubles to $14.5 billion as higher energy prices boost earnings
simplifiedContent: Exxon Mobil, a big oil company, just reported that it made $14.53 billion in profit in the second quarter of the year. This is more than double what it made in the same period last year. The company's revenue, which is the total amount of money it brought in, also increased by 42% to $116.02 billion. Higher oil prices and increased production helped the company make more money, even though there were some disruptions in the market. This matters because it shows that Exxon Mobil is doing well financially, which could be good news for people who invest in the company.

originalTitle: US stock market today: S&P 500, Nasdaq futures extend rally on strong tech earnings; Amazon up 13%
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening in the US stock market: technology stocks, like those of big companies, are doing well because they made more money than expected. This is helping the whole stock market, with Amazon's stock price going up 13%. However, even with this good news, the overall trend for July is not great, with the Nasdaq (a group of big technology stocks) expected to end the month 7% lower. Oil companies like Exxon and Chevron are also doing well because of higher oil prices, but investors are still being careful because of worries about global politics. Overall, it's a mixed situation with some positive signs, but also reasons to be cautious.

originalTitle: Maruti Suzuki Q1 Results: Net profit drops 9% as margin pressure offsets revenue growth; post-record sales
simplifiedContent: Maruti Suzuki, a car company, just released its financial results for the first quarter. Despite selling a record number of vehicles, the company's profit decreased by 9.1% compared to the same time last year. This is because the cost of making cars (like materials and labor) went up, which reduced the company's profitability. As a result, Maruti Suzuki had to raise the prices of its vehicles by up to ₹30,000 to try to maintain its profits. This matters because it shows that even with strong sales, a company's profits can still be affected by increasing costs.
